definition: Refract means to bend light or waves as they pass from one medium to another.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word refract. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know refract should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The telescope's cheap lens refracts blue more sharply than red, leaving a violet fringe around every star.
Deflect is a slighter departure than refract — a single nudge off course by anything in the way — while refract bends the wave by a fixed rule exactly where it crosses between two media.
Scatter goes further than refract — refracted rays bend together, by one rule, while scattered rays fly apart in every direction and the image is lost entirely.

Bend is the plain, all-purpose word for a change of path — a road, a wire, a beam of light, boundary or no boundary. Refract is the physics term for one specific bending: the swerve a wave makes exactly where it crosses from one medium into another.

Redirect means to send something along a new path by any means at all — a mirror, a wall, or a traffic cone will do the job. Refract names one mechanism only: the lawful bending that happens as light or sound passes across the boundary between two media.
